result.title: Formalizing Forgetting: Theory of Forgetting for Online Continual Learning
result.summary: Online continual learning (OCL) requires a learner to acquire a sequence of tasks in a single pass over the data, and catastrophic forgetting of earlier tasks remains its central challenge. Despite the many methods proposed to mitigate forgetting, the theoretical understanding of forgetting in OCL is still limited: existing analyses mostly focus on linear, overparameterized, or neural tangent kernel regimes, and it remains unclear which factors govern forgetting and how they affect it. To fill this gap, we analyze single-pass Shuffle SGD under strongly convex and general convex objectives and derive explicit upper bounds on the expected final forgetting. Further analysis of these bounds shows how the per-task data amount, task similarity, and task ordering enter them, and that their effects can differ across objective classes. Moreover, experiments with neural networks on Split-CIFAR-100 and PMNIST show that the trends suggested by our theory also appear in practice, indicating that these insights extend beyond the convex setting.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在强凸与一般凸目标下分析单遍 Shuffle SGD 的在线持续学习，给出期望最终遗忘量的显式上界，并讨论每任务数据量、任务相似度与任务顺序如何进入该上界，再用 Split-CIFAR-100、PMNIST 上的神经网络实验佐证趋势。
